question: Bengal Gazette, the first major newspaper in India, started in the year ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1780**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bengal Gazette** was the first major newspaper in India, marking the beginning of print journalism in the country.
 
• The paper was started by **James Augustus Hicky**, who is often referred to as the "father of Indian press".
 
• The first issue of Bengal Gazette was published on **29 January 1780**.
 
• The newspaper was also known as **Hicky's Gazette** and was characterized by its open criticism of the British Government in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **James Augustus Hicky:**

 
 
• James Augustus Hicky was an Irishman who launched the Bengal Gazette, the first English-language newspaper in India.
 
• He used the newspaper as a platform to criticize the policies and actions of the British East India Company and its officials.
 
• His outspoken nature and investigative journalism led to multiple legal issues with the British authorities.
 
• Despite his efforts to bring transparency, the newspaper was shut down by the British government in 1782.
 
 
 
• **History of Indian Journalism:**
 
 
• The Bengal Gazette paved the way for other publications in India, with newspapers becoming a significant medium for information and public discourse.
 
• In the early 19th century, several newspapers emerged, such as The Calcutta Journal, The Bombay Herald, and The Madras Courier.
 
• These publications played a crucial role in the Indian independence movement by spreading nationalist ideas and mobilizing public opinion against colonial rule.
 
 
 
• **Print Media Evolution:**
 
 
• The evolution of print media in India saw a transition from colonial-controlled press to a more diversified and free press post-independence.
 
• Post-independence, newspapers like The Times of India, The Hindu, and Indian Express became prominent in shaping public opinion and providing news coverage.
 
• Today, India's print media landscape includes a multitude of newspapers in various languages, catering to diverse audiences across the country.
